Summary: God's command to Jacob after twenty years with Laban: return to the land of his fathers and his kindred.
Commandment: Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.
Application: Parallels merged: the Genesis 31:3 command and the 31:13 repetition (arise, get thee out from this land) are one return journey commanded twice, not two returns. Jacob obeyed, and Laban pursued and then covenanted with him (Genesis 31:43-54).
Purpose: To bring Jacob back to the promised land with God's promised presence, ending his exile with Laban (Genesis 31:3).
Function: Twenty years with Laban, and then the word to go home. This was a one-time command, given once to Jacob for a specific moment, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not apply to it. Its goal was to bring Jacob back to the promised land with God's promised presence, ending his exile with Laban. The evil or restraint angle does not apply here; this was a return journey, not a law against a recurring evil. Jacob obeyed, and Laban pursued and then covenanted with him.
